name: friction_first
description: Short, conversational cold-email openers built around a specific current friction point and a likely business/user outcome.
opening_style: Open as a first-person surface check: I was checking out, I opened, I was looking at the App Store listing, or I was on the product website/app. Do not claim the sender downloaded or installed the app.
angle_priorities: Broken formatting, especially mobile layout issues.
Conversion friction such as unclear CTA, hidden signup/login, unnecessary onboarding steps, booking friction, checkout friction, or too many steps before value.
Weak proof, weak testimonials, weak case studies, external proof links, missing screenshots, or missing direct customer quotes.
Broad positioning or too many audiences/use cases when it likely hurts conversion.
App-store or public listing evidence only when it supports a specific activation/conversion/drop-off hypothesis.
Blog angles only when they directly reveal a positioning, onboarding, proof, or conversion issue.
preferred_phrases: I was checking out the [product] app...
I was looking at the [product] App Store listing...
qc_focus: One surface, one friction point, one outcome hypothesis.
Must flow naturally into a pitch about finding where users drop off and why.
Low-confidence visual findings need manual review before being treated as confirmed.
example_good_lines: I opened the fitrooms app listing and noticed the booking flow screenshots take a few taps before you see available slots, I'd guess that's costing bookings from users looking to book soon.

I was on the SleepWorks website and noticed the case study links go to external sources rather than direct customer quotes on the page, pulling those quotes closer to the CTA would likely lift conversion.
example_bad_lines: The product is powerful and could create a smoother experience.
I read your latest blog post and liked the way you explain the problem.
